Subject: Private Deploy: Account Setup & Network Validation Playbook

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To keep momentum toward your production cutover, I put together a concise playbook for the account/network prerequisites we need validated before we kick off the private deployment (VPC + on-prem option). The attached spreadsheet is the canonical checklist; below are the high-impact items we typically see as blockers so you can prioritize: 

High-priority items (please confirm status / owner):
- VPC peering or Transit setup: CIDR ranges, allowed routes, and who will configure route tables (Network team)
- Subnet design & ENI limits: dedicated subnets for inference nodes, NAT placement, and IP capacity for scale
- Firewall / ACL rules: outbound egress rules to allow model registry, telemetry, and Docker image pulls (list of egress endpoints in sheet)
- KMS / key access: service account principals that need decrypt/encrypt rights for model keys
- Service account / IAM: RBAC for Redwood runtime to pull images and write audit logs
- Certificate & PKI plan: internal certs for mTLS if you require private endpoints
- DNS & private zones: hostnames we will register and SRV records for autoscaling discovery
- Time sync / NTP: all nodes must have consistent clocks for trace correlation
- Proxy / outbound inspection: plan if your environment blocks direct egress — we'll need proxy host + auth method
- Audit log destination: S3/GCS bucket or SIEM ingest details and retention policy

Practical notes:
- We can work with your network team on a short RFC if you prefer.
- If you expect air-gapped installs, flag that now — the checklist diverges a bit (image import, local model registry).

Next steps I propose: you assign owners to the rows in the attached checklist and return the sheet with statuses by EOD Monday. Dev will run a quick environment validation once network access is confirmed.

Attaching: redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-item owners and test steps)

Thanks —
Rachel Kim

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the checklist — very actionable. Quick answers from our side: 
- VPC peering: Networking agrees to open a peer with the CIDR ranges you sent; they want the exact route map by Friday. Owner: Tim (cc'd).
- Subnets: We'll reserve a /22 for inference to start.
- Egress: We run a strict outbound inspection; we'll need the list of domains/IPs you require (can you confirm all telemetry and model registry endpoints?).
- KMS: We're using our centrally managed KMS. We need the service account email you'll use so we can grant decrypt perms.
- Air-gapped? Not for phase 1.

I'll assign owners in your spreadsheet and return it by tomorrow noon. Two asks from my infra lead: 1) can we get a sample validation script you run so we can dry-run behind our staging firewall, and 2) are there any special ports for health checks beyond 443/22?

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of IT Infrastructure — Greenfield Health
aisha.khan@greenfieldhealth.com | 617-555-0199

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private Deploy: Account Setup & Network Validation Playbook

Thanks Aisha — quick answers to the infra asks: 
- Validation script: attaching a compact checklist-runner (script stub in the spreadsheet). It checks TCP 443 outbound to our registry, validates NTP, and confirms KMS key access via a test decrypt. We'll provide a runnable shim you can execute in staging (no credentials baked in).
- Ports: default runtime uses 443 for control plane and 10250 for internal node health checks (Kubelet). If you're using a managed NAT with port restrictions, ensure 10250 is allowed between the control-plane subnet and worker subnets.
- Egress domains: added a short list in the sheet and an explicit CIDR/IP fallback for corporate proxies.

If Tim or network team want a short 30-min walkthrough of the validation steps, I can do it tomorrow afternoon.

— Dev
